## Verdict by claim

**Labelled doubly-principal scalar theorem — survives this audit.** For a finite countably additive complex measure with the prescribed complex cylinder values on the sigma-algebra generated by doubly-principal naturally labelled cylinders, existence iff `p ∈ [0,1]` is supported by a direct all-level variation argument. I found no counterexample or gap in the bound, endpoint treatment, or cylinder-algebra scope. This validates the stated scalar theorem, not global priority or a new general measure-extension criterion.

**Conditional covariant theorem — survives under its exact extra axiom.** The classification `0 < p ≤ 1` follows under (T) for every principal finite unlabelled shape, plus finite countable additivity and `ν(P∞)=1`. The all-principal scope of (T) is essential: if it is weakened to doubly-principal shapes only, the stated Dirac countermodel with `κ=0` works. Nothing here establishes an unconditional covariant extension theorem or derives (T) from covariance.

**Vector-valued scope — a material correction is needed in the adjacent vector-measure report.** The scalar result remains intact, but the infinite-dimensional norm-prescribed boundary has an explicit counterexample on the circle `|p|²+|1-p|²=1`. The `R²` infinite-extension question is not open outside the real segment: every countably additive finite-dimensional vector measure has finite total variation, so the level bound rules it out. See the concrete construction and report correction below.

**Novelty — no independent global priority verdict.** The selected theorem does solve the explicit doubly-reduced / doubly-principal inconclusive case identified by the 2023 source, but the derivation is elementary and uses the source’s known variation criterion. The repository’s manifest describes three native reviewers and explicitly says this was not a fresh two-family external review. Do not describe the adversarial gate as having passed an external model-diversity test.

## Independent scalar derivation and attempted defeaters

Let `a=|p|`, `b=|1-p|`, and, for `p∉[0,1]`, `t=a+b>1`, `r=a/t`, `s=b/t`. Both `a,b` are nonzero and `r,s∈(0,1)`. The equality case of the triangle inequality `|p|+|1-p|=1` is exactly the closed real segment, so the strict growth factor is valid for every excluded complex or real parameter.

A doubly-principal order on `k+2` labels has a unique last maximum and, after deleting it, a unique maximum at the preceding label. It is therefore uniquely `G ⊕ {u} ⊕ {v}` for an arbitrary naturally labelled `k`-order `G`. Conversely, these two caps make any `G` doubly principal. If `M(G)` is the number of maxima, the caps add `M(G)+1` links and no new incomparable pairs. Writing `w=L(G)+M(G)` and `h=binom(k,2)-R(G)`, the sum of moduli over the whole doubly-principal level is

`V_(k+2) = a Σ_G a^w b^h = a Σ_G t^(w+h) r^w s^h ≥ a t^k Σ_G r^w s^h`,

because each nonmaximal element is the lower endpoint of at least one cover, hence `w≥k`, and `h≥0`.

The remaining sum is not a heuristic estimate. In the independent-edge DAG on `k+1` ordered vertices with forward-edge probability `r`, a given transitive closure order `C` has probability `r^L s^(binom(k+1,2)-R)`: covers must be present, incomparable pairs must be absent, and redundant comparable edges sum out. Partition the event that the last vertex lies above every earlier vertex by the induced order `G` on the first `k` vertices. Its probability is exactly `Σ_G r^w s^h`. Reversing the order and exposing vertices outward, each new vertex connects to the already connected `j`-set with probability `1-s^j`; thus

`Σ_G r^w s^h = ∏_(j=1)^k (1-s^j) ≥ c_s := ∏_(j≥1)(1-s^j) > 0`.

The infinite product is positive because `0<s<1` and `Σs^j<∞` (for sufficiently small tail terms, `log(1-x)≥-2x`). Therefore `V_(k+2)≥a t^k c_s→∞`.

I tried the most likely proof failures: omitting labelled multiplicities, an off-by-one cap exponent, treating the two reachability events as independent, using the product at an endpoint where `s=0` or `1`, and transferring nonextension from the larger algebra by restriction. None applies. The proof does not assert a false equality after replacing `t^(w+h)` by `t^k`; it uses only a lower bound. It does not divide by `a` at `p=0`. The positive half uses ordinary transitive-percolation probability measures at `p=0` and `p=1` as deterministic endpoints and for `0<p<1` as usual.

The endpoints and dimensions are consistent: `G` has `k` labels; the doubly-principal endpoint has `k+2`; deleting its final label leaves the first cap as the unique maximum. At each fixed level, distinct naturally labelled finite orders have disjoint cylinder events. These cylinders lie in the target generated sigma-algebra, so their finite disjoint sums are bounded by total variation. Every countably additive complex-valued measure on a sigma-algebra has finite total variation; equivalently, this is the standard finite-complex-measure property used in the cited extension literature. Thus the unbounded level sums preclude the prescribed scalar complex measure.

The unlabelled regrouping in the conditional theorem is also correct: each shape `H` contributes exactly `N(H)` distinct natural-label representatives, all with the same `L`, `R`, and amplitude. No quotient by automorphisms should be applied to the labelled theorem’s level sum; `N(H)` is exactly the multiplicity needed when grouping that labelled sum into one covariant shape event.

## Conditional covariant proof and edge cases

The conditions are precisely stronger than the bare covariant problem: on `R_p`, require both `ν(Ω)=ν(P∞)=1` and one shape- and rank-independent finite `κ` satisfying `ν(D_H)=κ N(H)A_p(H)` for every principal `H`. Source Eq. (29) of Dowker–Zalel makes `D_H`, after intersection with `P∞`, a covariant event in the posts algebra; it need not be a raw labelled cylinder.

The normalization argument for `κ≠0` is valid and uses a real structural fact, not positivity of the complex measure. The countable family of all `D_H` covers `P∞`. At equal ranks distinct shapes are disjoint. For different ranks, the later post’s finite inclusive past fixes whether the earlier-rank post and its shape occurred; if so, transitivity and the later post’s future make the earlier post persistent throughout that event. Thus the family is laminar, and any finite intersection is empty or a family member. If `κ=0`, all family members have value zero; finite inclusion–exclusion gives zero to finite unions, and continuity from below then contradicts `ν(P∞)=1`. It would be invalid to infer that arbitrary zero-valued sets are null, but the proof does not do so.

For `p∉[0,1]`, `κ≠0` and the labelled level sum, grouped by unlabelled doubly-principal shape, gives disjoint rank-`n` event variation exactly `|κ|V_n(p)`, which diverges. For `p=0`, all principal `H` of size at least two have at least one cover and hence `A_0(H)=0`; their events still cover `P∞` because an infinite-post history has a post at some rank at least two. The same laminar-union argument contradicts normalization. For `0<p<1`, the real CTP measure supplies the factor `κ=∏(1-(1-p)^j)>0`; at `p=1`, the infinite chain supplies `κ=1`. The theorem’s `0<p≤1` endpoint is therefore correct.

The stated weakened-rule countermodel checks out. In the infinite ordinal sum of two-element antichains followed by singletons, each singleton is a post, while deleting the final post from its inclusive past leaves a latest two-element antichain, not a principal order. Therefore no post has a doubly-principal inclusive past, every doubly-principal `D_H` has Dirac measure zero, and the normalized Dirac measure satisfies the weakened doubly-principal-only rule with `κ=0`. It does not satisfy (T) for all principal `H`; this is exactly why it does not refute the conditional theorem.

The optional local-renewal paragraph also has the correct one-link ratio for principal `H`: a principal finite order has one maximum, so adjoining one new universal maximum adds one cover and changes amplitude by `p`. This check relies on restricting to principal `H`; it would be wrong for arbitrary nonprincipal `H`, where the number of new links is the number of old maxima.

## Vector-valued counterexample and report correction

Let `p` lie on the circle `|p|²+|1-p|²=1` and let `r=|p|²`, so `1-r=|1-p|²`. On the full labelled history space take ordinary real CTP probability `P_r`, set `H=L²(P_r)`, and define `μ(E)=1_E`. This is a countably additive Hilbert-space-valued measure: for disjoint `E_i`, the squared norm of the tail difference is `P_r(⋃_(i>N)E_i)→0`. For every finite labelled cylinder,

`||μ(cyl(C))||²=P_r(cyl(C))=r^L(1-r)^(binom(n,2)-R)=|A_p(C)|²`.

Restricting to the doubly-principal sigma-algebra preserves this equality. At `p=(1+i)/2`, `r=1/2`; this is a nonreal-parameter counterexample to any claim that the scalar modulus obstruction alone rules out all countably additive norm-prescribed vector extensions. It does not preserve the complex phases and therefore does not contradict the scalar theorem.

The vector measure has finite semivariation: every unit-norm scalarization is integration against some `g∈L²(P_r)` and its scalar total variation is at most `∫|g|dP_r≤||g||₂=1`. Its total variation is infinite, since at each level the disjoint cylinders have norm sum `V_n(p)→∞`. This distinction is impossible in finite dimensions: for a countably additive `R^d`-valued measure, each coordinate is a finite scalar measure and the vector total variation is bounded by the sum of coordinate variations. Therefore there is **no** countably additive `R²` extension for the nonreal case, even though the finite-level polygon construction exists.

Concrete correction to `research/extensions/vector-measure/AGENT_REPORT.md`: lines 74–89 should no longer call an infinite `R²` extension the remaining open problem; it is ruled out by finite-dimensional finite variation plus the already proved level bound. Lines 97–100 must narrow the finite-semivariation exclusion to finite dimensions. For infinite-dimensional targets, the `L²(P_r)` construction already supplies a finite-semivariation, infinite-total-variation extension on the circle. A different question could remain open away from that circle, or if the required vector assignment must retain phase information.

## Primary-source correspondence and verification

I read the project instructions, novelty sprint, verdict report, the full result and covariant theorem drafts, their fresh proof audit and the revision-cutoff manifest. I also reopened the primary sources at full-text depth (not abstract only):

- Dowker and Zalel, [arXiv:2212.01149v2](https://arxiv.org/html/2212.01149v2), §III.4, Eq. (26), and §V, Eqs. (29)–(30): confirms the CTP amplitude, the posts algebra, and the definition of doubly-principal generators as principal finite labelled orders whose penultimate restriction is principal. In §V the authors explicitly say their CTP extension test on this smaller tree is inconclusive, with the valency-one term left unresolved. This matches the target and does not already contain the all-level result.
- Surya and Zalel, [arXiv:2003.11311v1](https://arxiv.org/html/2003.11311v1), §2.3, Theorem 2.1 and Appendix B: the all-cylinder-algebra complex-measure criterion is bounded variation. It supports the scalar-measure variation premise, but does not itself classify a smaller doubly-principal sigma-algebra or supply amplitudes on missing cylinders.
- Bombelli, Seggev, and Watson, [arXiv:0809.2258v2](https://arxiv.org/html/0809.2258v2), §2, Theorem 2.1: gives the Euler-product post probability for real percolation and reports that almost-surely infinitely many posts is an Alon et al. result whose proof adapts to the one-sided process. The current conditional theorem labels this positive half as prior work. I did not independently retrieve the original Alon et al. proof, so that attribution remains a source-depth limit, not a contradiction found here.

I ran the existing bounded exact check `python3 research/creative/proof-audit/verify_small.py`. It passed its all-order endpoint-product checks for `k=0,…,4`, the two-cap checks, exact `Q(√2)` finite level sums, and older finite auxiliary checks. This is a consistency check only; the all-level conclusion comes from the analytic argument above.
